turn.subject: solution
turn.user_message: Yes — that’s exactly it. Show me what fixing it looks like.

text: Here’s what the fix is made of. It has five parts.
None of them needs a new hospital system on day one — they sit on top of how discharge runs today.
chat.pointer: Each part is shown with the question it answers. Pick the one you want to start with.
chat.note: Five parts, one aim: put the evening to work.
prompts: Which part saves the most time?
Do we need new hires for this?

blocks.title: What the fix is made of
blocks.deck: Five parts. Pick one to open it — they don’t need to go in order.

parts.title: Automations
parts.question: What does the software do so nobody works twice?
parts.detail: Captures the evening decision, drafts the summary, keeps a live bill and sends insurance pre-approval overnight.

parts.title: Process changes
parts.question: What changes on the ward, step by step?
parts.detail: The same steps, started in the evening and run side by side instead of one after another.

parts.title: Key people
parts.question: Who has to agree, and what do they give up?
parts.detail: Consultants, RMOs, nursing, billing, the TPA desk and housekeeping — with the COO approving the new order.

parts.title: Team & roles
parts.question: Do we need anyone new to own this?
parts.detail: One owner for discharge end to end, sized against your own peak hours rather than a flat ratio.

parts.title: KPIs & targets
parts.question: How will we know it worked?
parts.detail: A short list tied to your numbers. The ones nothing tracks today are marked as new.

stats.label: Average stay (ALOS)
stats.note: the measure the pilot will settle

blocks.caption: What all five parts are judged against.
